title: Comparative Status of Women in Vedic Civilization and Buddhism वैदिक सभ्यता र बौद्ध धर्ममा नारीहरूको तुलनात्मक स्थिति
nepali: सिद्धार्थ गौतमले बोधिज्ञान प्राप्त गरेपछि शाक्यमुनी बुद्ध बनेर विभिन्न मार्ग विकसित गर्ने क्रममा बढ्दासम्म पनि नारीलाई धर्म देशना गर्ने मार्ग खोलेका थिएनन् । ज्ञान प्राप्ति मार्गमा रहँदा भोकै बसेर मृत्युको मुखमा पुग्ने अवस्था हुँदा पनि सफलता नपाएपछि सुजाता नामक कन्याले दिएको पायस ग्रहण गरेर उरुबेलास्थित पिपल वृक्षमुनी बसेर थालेको ध्यान क्रममा आर्य सत्यहरूको साक्षात्कार सम्भव भएर शाक्यमुनी बुद्ध बनेपछि नारीप्रतिको धारणामा क्रमिक परिवर्तन हुँगै गएको थियो । त्यसपछि विस्तारै बौद्ध संघमा स्थान पाउन थालेका भिक्षुणीहरूले पनि आफ्ना संघ बनाएर मानसिक शान्ति एवं बौद्धिक विकासका मानक बनेर भूमिका निर्वाह गर्ने र स्थान बनाउने बाटो खुलेको हो । जसबाट वैदिक समाजमा रहेको नारीको महत्व पनि संरक्षित हुने अवस्थामा परिवर्तन आउने प्रवृत्तिसँगै बौद्ध संघमा भिक्षुणी संघलाई हेर्ने दृष्टिकोण पनि बदलिदै जान थाल्यो ।  अन्तमा केही मत भिन्नता उत्पन्न भए तापनि बौद्ध धर्ममा नारीहरूलाई मुक्ति प्राप्त गर्ने र स्वयंलाई संयोजित अर्थात् नियन्त्रित गरेर बढ्ने अवसर प्राप्त भयो । जसलाई नारी सशक्तीकरण तर्फको एक महत्त्वपूर्ण प्रयास पनि मान्न सकिन्छ ।
american_english: Even after Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment, became Shakyamuni Buddha, and progressed in developing various paths, he had not yet opened the path to preach the Dharma to women. When he failed to achieve success on the path of gaining knowledge despite fasting to the brink of death, he accepted rice pudding (payas) offered by a maiden named Sujata, and during the meditation he undertook while seated beneath the peepal tree at Uruvela, direct realization of the Noble Truths became possible; upon becoming Shakyamuni Buddha, a gradual transformation occurred in his perception of women. Thereafter, the avenue opened for nuns (bhikkhunis), who had gradually begun to gain a place within the Buddhist Sangha, to establish their own orders and carve out a role and standing as benchmarks of mental peace and intellectual development. Through this, along with the shifting tendency regarding the conditions under which the status of women in Vedic society was preserved, the perspective toward the Bhikkhuni Sangha within the Buddhist Sangha also began to change. Ultimately, despite some differences of opinion arising, women obtained the opportunity in Buddhism to achieve liberation and advance by disciplining—that is, controlling—themselves. This can also be considered an important endeavor toward women's empowerment.
british_english: Even after Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment, became Shakyamuni Buddha, and progressed in the course of developing various paths, he had not yet opened the path of expounding the Dhamma to women. When he achieved no success on the path to acquiring knowledge despite fasting to the point of being at death's door, he accepted the rice milk-pudding (payas) offered by a maiden named Sujata, and during the meditation he undertook whilst seated beneath the peepal tree at Uruvela, direct insight into the Noble Truths became possible; upon becoming Shakyamuni Buddha, a gradual transformation occurred in his attitude towards women. Thereafter, the avenue opened for nuns (bhikkhunis), who were gradually beginning to gain a place within the Buddhist Sangha, to establish their own communities and secure a role and standing as benchmarks of mental tranquility and intellectual development. Through this, along with the shifting tendency regarding the conditions under which the status of women in Vedic society was preserved, the perspective towards the Bhikkhuni Sangha within the Buddhist Sangha also began to alter. Ultimately, despite some differences of opinion arising, women obtained the opportunity in Buddhism to achieve liberation and advance by disciplining—that is to say, controlling—themselves. Which can also be regarded as an important endeavour towards women's empowerment.
australian_english: Even after Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment, became Shakyamuni Buddha, and moved forward in developing various paths, he had not opened up the path to preach the Dharma to women. After achieving no breakthrough on the path of gaining knowledge despite starving himself to the brink of death, he took the rice milk (payas) offered by a young woman named Sujata, and during the meditation he started while seated beneath the peepal tree at Uruvela, direct realization of the Noble Truths became possible; upon becoming Shakyamuni Buddha, a gradual shift took place in his attitude towards women. After that, the way opened up for nuns (bhikkhunis), who were gradually gaining a place in the Buddhist Sangha, to set up their own orders and forge a role and standing as benchmarks for mental peace and intellectual development. Through this, alongside shifts in the circumstances where the standing of women in Vedic society was maintained, the outlook towards the Bhikkhuni Sangha within the Buddhist Sangha also began to change. In the end, despite some differences of opinion cropping up, women gained the opportunity in Buddhism to attain liberation and progress by disciplining—that is, regulating—themselves. This can also be seen as an important step towards female empowerment.
informal_english: Even efter Siddhartha Gautama attained bodhi-knowledge, turned intae Shakyamuni Buddha, and went aboot developing different paths, he still hadnae opened up the way tae preach the Dharma tae women. Efter getting naewhere on the path tae knowledge despite starving himsel nigh on tae death, he took the rice pudding (payas) gien tae him by a lassie cried Sujata, and during the meditation he started sitting aneath the peepal tree at Uruvela, experiencing the Noble Truths firsthand became possible; once he became Shakyamuni Buddha, his view on women gradually began tae shift. Efter that, the gate opened for the nuns who were gradually finding a place in the Buddhist Sangha tae set up their ain orders and mak a name for themsels as benchmarks o mental peace and intellectual growth. Frae this, alongside shifts in how the standing o women frae Vedic society was kept up, the whole outlook toward the Bhikkhuni Sangha inside the Buddhist Sangha started changing an aw. At the end o the day, even wi a few disagreements cropping up, women got the chance in Buddhism tae win liberation and mak headway by disciplining—meaning keeping control o—themsels. Which can right well be taken as a right important step towards empowering women folk.
